title: Universal logic circuit for gate-controlled superconductor-based switches operating at liquid-helium temperatures
authors: Martin Berke, Lőrinc Kupás, Tosson Elalaily, Máté Sütő, Szabolcs Csonka, Péter Makk
abstract: The observation of the gate-controlled supercurrent (GCS) effect in superconducting nanostructures initiated major research efforts toward the realisation of superconducting-based computing architectures. Here we introduce a universal logic circuit that can be a promising superconducting building block of classical hybrid supercomputers. We demonstrate a functionally complete set of logic gates by realising the AND, OR, NOT and COPY gates. The general layout and scalability of our device, combined with recent experiments demonstrating fast switching and small voltage signals, make it a functional candidate in superconducting electronics. Our device enables the realization of all classical logic gates and the half-adder combinational logic circuit using at most three nanowires, each uniquely configured with two side-gate electrodes.
summary: The authors demonstrate a universal logic circuit by utilizing gate-controlled switches based on superconducting nanowires operating at liquid helium temperatures. By controlling the supercurrent via an applied gate voltage, they create reliable switching elements capable of implementing all classical logic gates (AND, OR, NOT) and combinational circuits. This work establishes a functional, scalable building block for future hybrid superconducting computers.
main_problem: Developing a superconducting building block for classical hybrid supercomputers due to scaling limitations and power consumption issues in conventional CMOS devices.
main_result: A universal logic circuit, realizing AND, OR, NOT, COPY gates, and the half-adder using only three gate-controlled superconducting nanowires was demonstrated.
method: The functionality is achieved by exploiting the Gate-Controlled Supercurrent (GCS) effect in superconducting nanowires, which acts as a voltage-controlled switch between superconducting and normal states.
model_or_system: The physical platform consists of superconducting nanowires (NbTiN) fabricated on silicon chips, controlled electrostatically via side-gate electrodes. Operation requires cryogenic temperatures ($	ext{T} \approx 4	ext{ K}$).
key_observables: Switching current ($I_{sw}$), critical current ($I_c$) vs. gate voltage ($V_{sg}$), and the resulting output voltage (high $\approx 2	ext{ V}$ in normal state, zero in superconducting state).
important_parameters: Operating temperature ($	ext{LHe}$), gate voltages ($	ext{V}_{	ext{g,onset}} \approx 30	ext{ V}$, $	ext{V}_{	ext{g,offset}} \approx 40	ext{ V}$), and bias currents ($I_b$).
main_assumptions: The logic operation relies on setting the bias current below the retrapping current during switching events; minor scattering is attributed to thermal fluctuations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $V$-$I$ curves showing gate-controlled switching (SC $\leftrightarrow$ N states) and time-domain plots demonstrating the truth tables for AND, OR, NOT, XOR, etc., gates using specific input/output voltage levels.
paper_structure: The paper systematically demonstrates the realization of basic logic gates (AND, OR, NOT, COPY) first, then expands to more complex combinational circuits like the half-adder and even a ring oscillator, proving the universality of the architecture.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses hardware implementation for classical computation using superconducting electronics, providing a solid experimental platform that could be relevant for developing control logic in quantum computing architectures.
